title: Interaction spec PRD and probe-driven acceptance playbook for hosted generation & embeddings
creator: Priya Nair
description: This PRD defines interaction-level behavioral specifications and a probe-driven acceptance playbook to validate chat/completions/embeddings/rerank hosted endpoints prior to broad rollout. It focuses on deterministic contracts (response shape, latency percentiles, quality regressions) and a lightweight probe harness that exercises cross-endpoint scenarios during canary slices.
context: Teams have observed subtle quality regressions when model variants or routing fallbacks are introduced. Existing unit and integration tests validate API surface and stability but miss cross-endpoint end-to-end behaviors (e.g., embeddings <-> rerank pipeline fidelity, chat fallback coherence). This work builds a repeatable acceptance layer that sits between PR-level tests and full production traffic.
scope_inclusions: Behavioral contract definitions for text generation (completions/chat) and embeddings + rerank call-chains
Probe harness that sends scripted and stochastic probes to hosted endpoints to assert contracts
Canary slice integration: run probes in the canary lane and surface pass/fail metrics in Console
Acceptance gating rules for automated rollout and rollback based on probe outcomes and SLOs
scope_exclusions: Large-scale load testing beyond canary slice (handled by SRE perf runbooks)
Changes to serving runtime internals (kernel selection, KV cache) — those remain engineering initiatives though will be consumers of this harness
Customer-facing SDK changes or public API surface modifications
requirements: Define a minimal set of behavioral assertions per endpoint: schema conformance, deterministic metadata fields, response time P50/P95 thresholds, and quality delta bounds against baseline prompts
Implement a probe harness that can: schedule probes, run deterministic assertion checks, run randomized fuzz probes (rate-limited), and emit structured telemetry compatible with Console dashboards
Integrate probes with canary lanes so each rollout executes the probe suite against the new variant and control variant in parallel
Create gating logic: block rollouts automatically if probe failure rate > 1% or quality delta > configured thresholds for three consecutive probe windows
Provide a short-form PRD and runbook for on-call and release engineers describing triage and rollback steps
Surface probe results and historical trends in Console per-route and per-model (token-level cost and probe pass/fail counts)
non_goals: Replacing existing eval pipelines — this is complementary and intentionally lightweight
Comprehensive adversarial safety testing — safety team retains responsibility for deep safety evals
Global rollout coordination beyond the initial hosted lanes and canary policy
success_metrics: Detect regressions pre-rollout: at least 90% of rollout-detected regressions should be caught by probes in canary slice
Reduce post-deploy behavioral incidents affecting customers by 40% in first quarter after rollout
Probe run time < 5s median per probe and < 30s for full suite during canary window
Acceptance gate false-positive rate < 2% (measured over 30 canary runs)
acceptance_criteria: Behavioral spec document approved by PM, an engineer from runtime team, and a Design/DEVEX reviewer
Probe harness deployed to canary lanes and executed automatically in at least two recent internal rollouts without causing instability
Console dashboard shows probe pass/fail, P50/P95 latencies, and quality-delta signals for the canary variant and control
Automated gating prevents promotion of a variant that fails probe thresholds in two consecutive windows
Triage runbook validated in a simulated failure (chaos simulation or staged regression) and documented incident timeline
launch_checklist: Finalize behavioral assertions and baseline prompt set (owns: PM + Applied ML)
Implement probe harness MVP and open-source internal library for orchestration (owns: infra-engineering)
Add telemetry ingest and Console visualizations (owns: observability)
Hook probes into canary lane pipeline and enable gating feature flag (owns: deployment-team)
Dry-run probes against staging and record false-positive/negative counts (owns: QA)
Security review and data retention policy confirmed for probe payloads (owns: Security)
Operational runbook, escalation contacts, and rollback playbook published in Confluence (owns: PM)
Sign-off meeting with Product, Runtime, Observability, and SRE prior to enabling gating in production (owners: PM + Eng managers)
rollout_steps: 1) Deploy probe harness to canary lane behind feature flag; run in read-only mode to collect telemetry for two days
2) Validate dashboard and thresholds with product and applied-ML stakeholders; tune thresholds as needed
3) Enable automated gating for a small internal canary slice (1% traffic) for 72 hours
4) Expand canary slice to 10% if probe pass rate remains green and no customer-impact incidents reported
5) Full promotion with gradual traffic ramp to 100% using existing rollout policies; keep probes running for 30 days post-promotion
